title: Natural selection is the main but not exclusive means of modification

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Natural selection is the main but not exclusive means of modification

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Natural selection has been the main, but not the only, cause of the modification of species.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Furthermore, I am convinced that Natural Selection has been the main but not exclusive means of modification.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), the Introduction; section “Introduction”. Scope: all organic beings

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-intro-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.46

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Mechanism-specific evidence exists, but aggregating all species modification into comparable causal shares is not currently possible. Existing data resolve selected lineages and traits only.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For many lineages, estimate the share of heritable phenotypic and genomic change attributable to positive or purifying selection versus drift, gene flow and other mechanisms. A majority attributable to selection would support 'main,' whereas consistently minority contributions would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Main' lacks a unique denominator.

Selection and demography can produce similar genomic signals.

Available taxa are highly biased.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Sequence archives make a neutrality-versus-selection contrast routine for genes, and that contrast can show that selection is not the sole process. They do not measure the share of organismal modification caused by selection across living things. Several defensible partitions give different answers, and assembling a phenotypic sample would take months of harmonization for a still-narrow subset.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Partition evolutionary change in form among selection, drift, and other inheritance systems, using quantitative-genetic and comparative estimates, and treat sequence substitution rates only as a modern side test. Selection would count as the main cause if it explained more of the phenotypic change than drift, mutation bias, and plasticity combined, while still leaving a non-zero residue for other causes; a predominance of neutral or plastic change would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Main cause of modification' needs an agreed currency that sums across traits, species, and timescales.

Estimates of selection on phenotypes are scattered through papers and cover a tiny slice of traits.

Darwin's modification is change of organisms, so a molecular neutrality test answers a reinterpreted question.
